summary: 2fa-secretkey postinstall harvests Minecraft/browser credentials to XOR-obfuscated Discord webhook
details: Package advertises itself as a zero-dependency TOTP helper but ships a postinstall payload that steals credentials from the installer's Windows machine. package.json's postinstall requires./lib/core, whose top-level code (gated by a sandbox/CI evasion check on CI, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, JEST_WORKER_ID, npm_config_global, APPDATA/USERPROFILE/USERNAME/COMPUTERNAME, npm_lifecycle_script containing 'audit'/'pack', and the presence of %USERPROFILE%\Documents) reads Minecraft launcher refresh tokens from Windows Credential Manager entries (MCL|*|Xal.*) and from.minecraft account JSON files, and decrypts Chromium-based browser secrets by shelling out to PowerShell to call System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData::Unprotect on the Chrome Local State encrypted_key and then AES-256-GCM decrypting stored passwords/cookies. The harvested data (including attached files with an @everyone mention) is POSTed to a hardcoded Discord webhook whose URL, along with the strings 'powershell', 'child_process', 'ProtectedData', and 'Add-Type', is XOR-0x3F obfuscated and reconstructed at runtime by a small decoder function _x. None of this behavior has any relationship to TOTP generation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
